compatible_reusable_primitives: strict spec and done provenance identity

overlap_and_risks.finding: v2.2 dispatch/watchdog and detached v3 controller independently own worker lifecycle; two writers/watchdogs can race.
v3 allows retries of same spec up to 3; v2.2 permits no repetition of failed route and only 2 distinct preregistered equivalent routes.
v3 worker uses start_new_session and detached bootstrap; wrapping v3 controller inside the v2.2 watchdog is not a demonstrated kill-tree guarantee.
v3 controller returns 0 for RUNNING/BUSY, not only PASS. v2.2 must never treat a controller-exit 0 as completed output.
Old V255 operational checkpoint receipt is historical; V259 on current main and v2.2 pointer must be re-read before binding.

minimal_route: Retain v2.2 as sole dispatcher/watchdog/process owner. Reuse v3 validation and log-cap primitives only after extraction without launching its detached controller. Require pinned one-stage plan, bounded process ownership and independent kill/restart tests. Keep v3 opt-in and isolated.
next_action: Prototype a single-owner bounded local worker adapter on a current-main-derived engineering branch; add adversarial tests for orphan, double dispatch, separate process group escape, identity drift and non-repeat. No v3 recursive kernel activation until proven.
